features.name: Nothing published until both sign-offs are green
features.label: nothing published until both are green
features.promise: A publish cannot proceed until both the code review (screens 11 and 12) and the outcome sign-off (screen 13) have passed, and the publish carries both.
features.howToVerify: With a change whose code review is approved but whose outcome sign-off is not (and again with the reverse), open the publish step on screen 07 and confirm the destination choices cannot be committed; approve the second one and confirm the same publish then proceeds and shows both sign-offs attached.
features.notes: Flow map edge label 43:91 and the "Choose where it goes" caption 43:40 "Both sign-offs attached".
features.evidence: Walked base's publish dialog through four gate states this round and the two destinations that cross the gate were refused in every one of them. 'Never handed over' before a packet existed; 'Outcome sign-off outstanding' with only the code approved ('The code review is signed off by Default Admin. The outcome sign-off on packet 1 is still outstanding.'); 'Changes requested' after I handed the criteria list back; 'Sign-offs are stale' once the tree moved past the packet ('any sign-off on record is about a different change'). In all four the 'Push to an OCI repository' and 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' rows render with no checkbox at all - `[data-testid=barn-publish-target-oci]` and `-repository` matched 0 - so they cannot be committed, and the submit stayed disabled at 'Pick a destination'. The dialog also states the rule beside them: 'Two people answer two questions, and only leaving the gate - putting the packet where people who did not build it can install it - asks for them.' What I could not show is the positive half (the same publish then proceeding), because the OCI push is not built and the repository route needs a GitHub token this Studio has no way to obtain; both rows say so in their own words rather than pretending.

features.name: The brief sits on the main path before the build
features.label: Agree the brief — The need, the open questions, the criteria · Screen 10
features.promise: Agreeing the brief is a required stage between describing what you want (screen 02) and building it (screen 03), unlike checking the diff yourself (screen 04), which is explicitly optional.
features.howToVerify: Create a new extension from screen 02 and confirm the route passes through the brief on screen 10 before the workspace on screen 03; confirm by contrast that screen 04 can be skipped.
features.notes: Flow map: green connectors 43:50 and 43:53 put 43:11 between 43:8 and 43:16 on the main path, while 43:21 marks screen 04 "Optional". Rationale row 44:41: "It is only cheap to catch before the code exists".
features.evidence: Created an extension from screen 02 (description, outcome, name 'w6bvc', placement 'Inside a cluster'). The submit button is literally labelled 'Draft the brief', and pressing it created the pod and routed to /dashboard/barn/extensions/w6bvc/brief?prompt=...&outcome=...&placement=c-cluster, with what I typed carried into the brief's own fields ('## What you were handed' held the description verbatim). So the brief sits between describing and building. By contrast screen 04 is reachable but skippable - it offers 'Back to assistant' and reverting per file, signs nothing and blocks nothing - and the brief itself offers 'Skip the brief', which is a deliberate bypass rather than the default. I deleted the extension I created (deployment, service and both ConfigMaps).

features.name: No capability of the current build is lost
features.label: Keeps everything the current build does: CLI, files, GitHub import, publish, settings.
features.promise: The redesign is additive: the CLI, the files view, GitHub import, publish and settings all remain available, and the raw terminal output in particular is still reachable one click away and still the source of truth.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each of the five capabilities is still reachable in the running Studio, and that the raw assistant output is reachable in one click from the activity stream on screen 03.
features.notes: Cover point one (29:13); rationale row 27:16 "Raw output is still there, one click away, and still the source of truth".
features.evidence: Re-drove all five against the installed bundle, because this round changed the hand-over path, the publish summary, the masthead and the shared scanners. CLI: 'Show raw output' [data-testid=barn-open-raw-output] expands in one click and renders the pod's real log - I read 'DONE Compiled successfully in 3457ms', 'App running at: - Local: http://localhost:8005' and a later 'WAIT Compiling...1:58:41 AM' out of it, with timestamps that match the pod's actual dev server, and the panel says 'the terminal is still here'. The Terminal tab attaches a live xterm (canvas present) to the pod's tmux session, and I read my own prompts back out of it with `tmux capture-pane -t mc-editor` five separate times during this run. FILES: /barn/extensions/base/files lists the tree with branches and last-commit information and opens a file. GITHUB IMPORT: the Import dialog does connection as step 1 inline ('you can paste it here without losing what you have typed'), with no link out to settings. PUBLISH: the dialog renders all five destinations with their gates. SETTINGS: /barn/settings renders connection, the sign-off matrix, permissions, access and data. The masthead change did not cost anything - the editor gear that used to open a second token modal is gone and nothing else went with it; the raw-output button and the Terminal tab are both still one click from the assistant panel.

features.name: A requested change arrives as an assistant instruction
features.label: Goes straight back to the workspace with the comment already loaded into the assistant — the reviewer never writes the fix themselves
features.promise: A reviewer's comment, from either the code review or the outcome sign-off, is carried into the author's workspace already loaded into the assistant as the instruction to work from, and the reviewer is never asked to write the fix.
features.howToVerify: Comment on a hunk on screen 12 and use "Send to the assistant", then open the author's workspace on screen 03 and confirm the reviewer's exact wording is present as a pending assistant instruction that the author must still approve.
features.notes: Flow map "Changes requested" (43:44/43:46) is fed by amber arrows from both "Code review" (43:82) and "Outcome sign-off" (43:85); rationale row 44:32 adds "the author still approves it".
features.evidence: Both routes, both landing in the same place, both with the reviewer's own wording. From a hunk on screen 12: opened the composer on line 1, typed 'W6BVC cross probe: rename this probe file before merging.' and pressed 'Send to the assistant' - the pod's tmux pane then held 'A reviewer looked at this change and asked for something. It is about verify-w6bvc-scope.ts around line 1. Their words: W6BVC cross probe: rename this probe file before merging.. Make that change in the working tree and explain what you did.' From the decision bar: 'Request changes' opened a modal that says what it does ('recorded against the code review... also put straight to the assistant working in base's pod, so the change is made by the thing that wrote it rather than by you'), and sending it recorded changes-requested in the review record and routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the terminal attached and the paragraph already in the session. The reviewer writes a sentence, never a fix, and the author still has to act on it.

features.name: One diff against the last published version
features.label: collapsed into one diff against the last published version
features.promise: The reviewer is shown a single diff of the change against the last published version, not the sequence of intermediate edits that produced it.
features.howToVerify: Make an edit and then undo or supersede it before pushing, then open the change on screen 12 and confirm the diff shows only the net difference from the last published version and no intermediate state.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.evidence: Screen 12 measures from the last published version and says so out loud. With one uncommitted file in base the header read 'Reviewing all 1 file' and the narrowing sentence read 'Showing what has landed since <sha>, the commit you last read... The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 1 file. Approve still commits all of it.' The intermediate history is not shown: I made three commits into base during this run (two hand-over sweeps and a review commit) and the review screen never listed them as steps - it showed the net difference only. Screen 04 says the same thing about the same baseline ('Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree.').

features.name: Connection state and permission mode are one state shown in two places
features.label: Connection state is a persistent strip in the panel: a dot, the account, and the permission mode as a real control.
features.promise: The account, connection state and assistant permission mode shown on the workspace strip (screen 03) and on the settings page (screen 09) are the same state, and settings is the one place all of it lives.
features.howToVerify: Change the permission mode on screen 09 and confirm the workspace strip on screen 03 reflects it without a reload, and vice versa; confirm no other modal edits the GitHub token.
features.notes: Rationale rows 27:25 ("Screens 03, 09") and 27:34; caption 23:918 "connection, permissions, access and data in one place", replacing the bare token modal (23:919).
features.defect: The permission mode is not one state in two places and cannot be. Screen 03's chip reports the live session ('Planning only, no edits'); screen 09 reports the mode the pod starts in ('Edits apply without asking'), and marks the radio group not settable. The two disagreed on screen while I looked at them. What changed this round is that neither screen pretends otherwise: [data-testid=barn-permission-split] on screen 03 spells the divergence out ('Two readings of two different things, and neither screen can change the other'), and [data-testid=settings-permission-fixed] explains that the pod starts claude with --dangerously-skip-permissions from a ConfigMap the bundle rewrites on every page load, so a level chosen on the page would be undone within seconds. Honest, but the rule asks for one state settable in one place, and that is not what exists.
features.evidence: Judged as two halves, because they now behave differently. CONNECTION: passes. Screen 03's strip [data-testid=barn-session-state] reads 'The assistant is not signed in . run /login in the terminal', and screen 09's [data-testid=settings-assistant-login] reads 'The assistant is not signed in', with the detail row naming every pod it asked ('No credential in any of these pods (base, demo, nodehealth, v6r)... and the workspace's own session strip says the same'). Both come from the same `assistantLogin()` reading of the pod, so they are one state in two places. The GitHub side agrees too: settings names the account ('Not connected'), and the editor masthead's gear that used to open a second bare token modal no longer exists - `grep -rn barn-editor-settings-button --include=*.vue` finds only a comment. The remaining EditorSettingsModal openings are inline in flows with something in flight (the create form, the import dialog, the hand-over), which is what the design's own rationale row asks for, and they write through the same connectGithub into the same Secret. PERMISSION: still fails, and the product now says why rather than hiding it.

features.name: Verification walks the criteria written in the brief
features.label: Acceptance criteria written in the brief become a checklist walked against the running build, with captured evidence and a second, separate sign-off.
features.promise: The acceptance criteria are authored once on screen 10 and are the same items walked, against the running build and with evidence captured, on screen 13.
features.howToVerify: Write a distinctive acceptance criterion in the brief on screen 10, take the change through to verification, and confirm screen 13 lists that exact criterion as a checklist item, exercised against the running build, with the captured evidence attached.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59 ("Screens 07 and 13"); caption 45:1206 "the criteria walked against the running build"; flow map 43:37.
features.evidence: Authored once, walked once, on an extension I created for the purpose so nothing else could account for it. Wrote 'W6BVC MARKER: the trend panel names the window it covers' into the first acceptance criterion on screen 10 for w6bvc; the page saved it ('Saved 02:18 AM') and BRIEF.md in that pod gained '- [ ] W6BVC MARKER: the trend panel names the window it covers' under '## How we will know it worked'. Screen 13 for the same extension then listed exactly that one criterion, with Yes / No / Can't tell / Show me against it, and nothing was re-entered anywhere. I then exercised it against the running build: 'Show me' drove the pinned preview (that pod's own dev server through the apiserver proxy) to /home and 'Capture this as evidence' wrote '- Captured 2026-08-24 02:19 by Default Admin at `/home`' into the file under that criterion. So the criterion, the walk and the evidence are one chain through three screens.

features.name: Built from components the dashboard already has
features.label: Everything below is achievable with components that already exist in the Rancher dashboard — SortableTable, LabeledInput, Banner, Card, Tabbed, AsyncButton — so none of this asks the team to invent new UI primitives.
features.promise: Every screen is realisable with existing Rancher dashboard primitives, and the Studio home list in particular uses the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page rather than a bespoke table.
features.howToVerify: Inspect the rendered markup of the Studio screens and confirm tables, inputs, banners, cards, tabs and async buttons are the dashboard's own components rather than reimplementations, and that screen 01 reads like the Clusters page table.
features.notes: Header note 27:5 of the rationale frame; rationale row 27:88 names the Clusters page pattern for screen 01.
features.defect: Screen 01 is a bespoke table, not the SortableTable pattern the rationale row names ('the same SortableTable pattern as the Clusters page'), so the claim that a Rancher user already knows how to read it does not hold. The wider claim is met in spirit (nothing needs a new primitive) but not in fact (the primitives are new implementations of existing ones). Recorded as a deliberate departure in DEPARTURES.md section 1, with the cost it has already had.
features.evidence: Inspected the rendered markup of the Studio screens again. The Studio is built from its own S-prefixed primitives in pkg/barn/components/ui (SButton, SChip, SBanner, SCard, STabs, SMenu, SModal, SField). On screen 01, document.querySelectorAll('.sortable-table') is 0, and the table is a div grid: .studio-home__table with hand-rolled .studio-home__th headers (State, Name, Source, Running on, Last change). None of Rancher's own component classes appear either - .labeled-input 0, .banner 0, .async-button 0, .tabbed 0.

features.name: A guaranteed way back from any build failure
features.label: When it breaks — plain-language cause, one-click fix, guaranteed way back
features.promise: Every build is snapshotted so that a failure always has a state to roll back to, which means the snapshot has to be taken in the workspace before the change that breaks it.
features.howToVerify: Cause a build to fail from a known-good state and confirm screen 08 offers a snapshot of that state to roll back to, and that rolling back returns the workspace to it.
features.notes: Caption 23:915 and rationale row 27:97 "a snapshot to roll back to"; the snapshot is created on screen 03 and consumed on screen 08.
features.evidence: Seeded a recorded failure and opened screen 08. It named the cause in words, was honest that it had pattern-matched the log rather than understood it, and offered 'Ask the assistant to explain this', 'Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue' and, for the way back, 'Roll back to the snapshot "autosave 0217 on Aug 24"' taken three minutes earlier, with 'Undo the last change' beside it and '0 changed files since'. The snapshots are real: refs/tags/barn-snap/* in base's pod holds dozens of automatic ones. The screen is also honest about the limit of the guarantee ('A snapshot is a point somebody chose, not necessarily a build that worked') and says rolling back snapshots the failed tree first so nothing is lost.

features.name: Iteration before the gate asks nobody
features.label: Iteration is completely ungated: dev preview and developer load ask nobody.
features.promise: Creating, building, previewing, breaking, rebuilding and developer-loading an extension never require anyone's approval, so no review or sign-off control may block any of them.
features.howToVerify: Make several edits in the workspace (screen 03), let a build fail and recover it (screen 08), and developer-load the result, confirming that no approval dialog, pending-review banner or disabled control appears at any point before screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 65:1083; flow map caption 43:18 "Readable activity, live preview, and no gates at all" and 43:24 "Everything before it is yours alone".
features.evidence: Everything I did before the publish dialog asked nobody, across four extensions and roughly two hours. Created an extension from screen 02, drafted and edited its brief, agreed one brief and skipped another, added and answered questions, planted and edited files in a pod, ran the scope checks, commented on a hunk and sent it to the assistant, requested changes, opened the failure screen and read its rollback offer, walked verification and signed it off. No approval dialog, no pending-review banner and no disabled control appeared at any point. The only gate chips in the product are on the two distribution rows of the publish dialog; 'Load into this Rancher' and 'Push the source to GitHub' are both chipped 'No sign-off', and settings' [data-testid=settings-iteration-note] says the same in policy terms.

features.name: The OCI publish gate
features.label: Push to an OCI repository — The one hard gate. Everything before it is yours alone · Screen 07
features.promise: There is exactly one hard gate in the whole product and it is the push to an OCI repository, the point at which the extension first becomes installable by other people.
features.howToVerify: From a freshly created extension, walk stages 01, 02, 10, 03 and 04 without ever being asked for an approval, then start a publish to an OCI repository on screen 07 and confirm that this is the first and only step that will not complete on the author's say-so alone.
features.notes: Flow map 43:22/43:24 and the guardrail note 43:93; rationale row 65:1083 states it as "The gate is the push to an OCI repository, where the extension first becomes installable by other people".
features.evidence: The publish dialog names exactly one hard gate and puts it at the distribution boundary: 'Push to an OCI repository. The gate. The one hard gate in the design: the point an extension becomes installable by people who did not build it, and the only step that asks anybody for permission.' 'Put the reviewed packet on the repository' is tagged 'The gate' as the same boundary by the route this Studio can take. Beside them 'Load into this Rancher' is chipped 'No sign-off' and reversible, and 'Push the source to GitHub' is chipped 'No sign-off' because it is how you ask for a review rather than how you leave the gate. Nothing earlier in the walk (01, 02, 10, 03, 04) asked for an approval. The OCI push itself is not built and the row says so plainly rather than drawing a button that lies.

features.name: The hand-off to review is a PR, and the PR is the record
features.label: hand-off · the PR is the record
features.promise: Crossing the gate hands the work from the author's lane to the reviewers' lane by producing a PR, and that PR is the durable record of the hand-off.
features.howToVerify: Push a change to an OCI repository and confirm the resulting queue entry on screen 11 is backed by a PR, and that the PR is reachable from the review surface as the record of the change.
features.notes: Flow map connector label 43:90 on the green connector running from "Push to an OCI repository" (43:22) into "Code review" (43:28).
features.evidence: Drove the whole hand-off. In the pod: refs/barn/packets/2 and branch barn/demo/2 at 2883651, plus the review record entry in ConfigMap barn-review-demo carrying repo codyrancher/trash and pr {number:1, url:...}. On GitHub: the branch exists and PR #1 is open against main, its body written by handOverForReview ('Handed over from the Rancher Extension Studio as packet 2', collapsed against 288365169a2a, the two outstanding sign-offs, and the no-brief paragraph). packetPullRequest('demo') answered state recorded, sentence 'Packet 2 was handed over as pull request #1.' Screen 11's demo row reads 'Handed over as packet 2 1 minute ago by Default Admin. As pull request #1.' and carries a PR #1 field. Screen 12's chip reads 'PR #1 opened'. publishSummary put 'packet 2 on barn/demo/2, pull request #1' on the status strip rather than the old 'in this cluster only'. The previous fail (no token) no longer holds.

features.name: Preview and published are separated by an explicit line
features.label: The same live preview, plus an explicit boundary: preview is yours alone, snapshotted per build, and publishing is a separate deliberate act.
features.promise: Work in the live preview affects only the author and is snapshotted per build; nothing reaches anyone else until the separate, deliberate publish on screen 07.
features.howToVerify: Make a visible change in the workspace preview on screen 03, then confirm from another session or another user that the installed extension is unchanged until a publish is performed on screen 07.
features.notes: Rationale row 27:52 ("Screens 03, 07"); the cover's reading note 29:41 calls it "an explicit line between preview and published".
features.evidence: base had a dirty working tree and a live preview throughout this run and none of it reached anybody: `kubectl get uiplugins -A` lists only barn and nodehealth, and base's row on screen 01 offers 'Remove the local install' greyed out with the reason 'not installed'. Screen 04 says the same in words: 'Nothing here has reached the repository yet. Everything here is in the pod's working tree. Publishing builds from it; discarding puts it back to the last commit.' Publishing is a separate deliberate act in a dialog where every destination is unticked and the submit reads 'Pick a destination' until you choose one. Snapshots are taken per build - refs/tags/barn-snap/* in the pod, the newest three minutes old when screen 08 offered it.

features.name: Prompt provenance and the brief survive from authoring into review
features.label: Every hunk carries the prompt that produced it, and the whole change carries its brief.
features.promise: The prompt that caused each hunk is captured during authoring on screen 03 and is still attached, per hunk, when the change is reviewed on screen 12, and the brief from screen 10 travels with the change as a whole.
features.howToVerify: Author a change with two distinguishable prompts in the workspace, push it, then on screen 12 confirm each hunk shows the prompt that produced it and that the change header shows the brief written on screen 10.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:5; caption 45:1204 "prompt provenance per hunk".
features.defect: Same root cause as 12-change-hunk-provenance: barn-provenance.mjs and shell.sh pick the first directory under /app/pkg, which in demo's pod is base rather than demo, so the turn commits and the blame index are built against a tree no review screen reads. Secondary: assemblePacket sets turnsSince to state.baseAt, and state.base falls back to HEAD when no baseline ref exists, so the accumulated-prompt window is empty for any extension that has never been published locally - packet 2 recorded turns: 0 despite three real turns minutes earlier. The previous verdict blamed the missing credential; with the credential present the credential is no longer the reason.
features.evidence: The authoring half now works: three prompts sent from the composer on screen 03 were captured in /app/.barn/provenance.jsonl with screen 'workspace', principal local://user-btc48 and 'Default Admin', two of them ending in commits whose messages carry Barn-Turn, Barn-Session, Barn-Origin and Barn-Principal trailers, and a PostToolUse touch record per Edit. The per-hunk half does not survive into screen 12: the hunk's strip says 'This file is not in the provenance report'. Packet 2's own note recorded turns: 0, because turnsSince is set to the base commit's timestamp and the base is HEAD (no refs/barn/published/* exists until something is published locally), so every turn that produced the change falls outside the window the packet records.

features.name: Live is reversible from the extension list
features.label: Reversible from the extension list
features.promise: Publishing is not a one-way door: a live extension can be taken back from the Studio home list on screen 01.
features.howToVerify: Publish an extension, return to /dashboard/barn/extensions, and confirm the row for the live extension offers a way to reverse the publish.
features.notes: Flow map terminal state "Live" (43:41) and its caption 43:43; the reversal control lives on screen 01, not on screen 07.
features.evidence: Opened the row menu on /barn/extensions. nodehealth, which is installed as a UIPlugin (cattle-ui-plugin-system/nodehealth v0.1.0), offers an enabled 'Remove the local install v0.1.0' alongside 'Open in the workspace', 'Review changes', 'Open files' and 'Open the brief'. base and the others, which are not installed, show the same item with the reason on it. So the list is where a live extension is taken back, and the item states its own applicability rather than being hidden.

features.name: Every recovery route returns to the same workspace
features.label: amber is recovery — and every recovery route leads back into the same workspace rather than out of the product
features.promise: Both failure routes drawn on the map, a broken build and a rejected review, end back in the author's workspace rather than in a separate remediation surface or outside the product.
features.howToVerify: Trigger a build failure and apply its fix, confirming the user lands back in the same workspace; separately, request changes as a reviewer and confirm the author is returned to that same workspace rather than to a new screen.
features.notes: Flow map legend 43:4; the amber arrows 43:62/43:65 leave and re-enter the same "Build it and watch it" box (43:16), and "Changes requested" (43:44) routes back to it.
features.evidence: Both amber routes end in the same workspace, and I drove both. Rejection: 'Request changes' on screen 12 routed me to /dashboard/barn/editor/base?tab=terminal with the xterm attached and the reviewer's paragraph already in the session, not to a remediation screen. Build failure: screen 08's actions are all workspace actions ('Ask the assistant to fix it', 'Undo the last change', 'Roll back to the snapshot "autosave 0217 on Aug 24"', 'Show me pages/NodeHealth.vue'), and its copy is about returning the same tree rather than branching out of the product. Screen 13's two send-back actions do the same thing by prompt: both put their text into the same pod session. Neither route left the Studio.

features.name: The review packet accumulates in the background and is assembled at the push
features.label: the review packet accumulates quietly in the background. It is only assembled and handed to a reviewer at the push to a repository
features.promise: Everything a reviewer will need is captured continuously while the author works, but it is only assembled into a review packet and handed over at the moment of the push.
features.howToVerify: Work in the workspace for several build cycles without publishing and confirm nothing appears in the review queue (screen 11), then push once and confirm a complete packet, including material captured across all of those earlier cycles, appears in a single queue entry.
features.notes: Guardrail note 43:93 on the flow map.
features.evidence: Both halves now hold, and the accumulation is a reading rather than a claim. While I worked in base without publishing, the assistant panel on screen 03 carried [data-testid=barn-review-accumulation] and the publish dialog carried the same sentence with numbers in it: 'Since packet 1 was handed over, 0 commits, 1 file, 2 recorded prompts have accumulated in the pod. None of it is in anybody's review queue: it is assembled into packet 2 and handed over at the push, and not before.' Nothing appeared in the review queue during any of that - screen 11 lists only handed-over extensions and says so in its empty state. Pressing the hand-over then assembled it in one go: packet 2 was written with turns: 2 and the window turnsSince it counted over, and screen 12 read it back as '3 prompts were gathered behind packet 3 since 2026-08-24T01:17:09.000Z. The pod still holds exactly what packet N was assembled from, so the diff below and the packet are the same change.' I repeated the cycle for packet 3 and the counts moved with the work. One defect found on the way, worth recording even though it does not break the rule: assemblePacket's `git update-ref refs/barn/packets/<n>` is `;`-chained ahead of `echo BARN-PACKET-OK` and carries no `2>&1`, so when that refs directory was root-owned (left that way by an earlier verifier's root-level git command) the ref write failed with 'Permission denied', the failure was swallowed, and the hand-over reported success while writing a record naming a ref that did not exist. I chowned the directory back to uid 1000 and the same hand-over then wrote the ref correctly. The other write in that chain uses `2>&1`; this one does not.

features.name: The build is compared back to its own brief at sign-off
features.label: The build is compared back to its own brief, and anything outside it is flagged during sign-off — accept it into the brief, or take it out.
features.promise: At outcome sign-off the built change is diffed against the brief that started it, and anything not in the brief is surfaced with two resolutions: accept it into the brief, or remove it.
features.howToVerify: Have the assistant make a change beyond what the brief asked for, take it to screen 13, and confirm the extra work is flagged as outside the brief and offers both accepting it into the brief and taking it out.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:68; requires the screen 10 brief to still be attached to the change at screen 13.
features.evidence: Planted a file in base's pod whose added line mentions three of the terms the brief's '## What we are deliberately not doing' uses ('alerting', 'history', 'beyond'). Screen 13's Scope card flagged it automatically, named the file per term, and offered both resolutions as real buttons. 'Remove it' put the behaviour to the assistant in the pod with the coincidence caveat and left BRIEF.md byte-identical. 'That is fine - add it to the brief' opened a plan showing exactly what would move, and confirming it rewrote BRIEF.md so the sentence left the non-goals and arrived under 'What changes for them' stamped '(accepted during verification on 2026-08-24 by admin)', with the rest of the sentence left ruled out; the warning then cleared for those terms. [data-testid=verify-scope-limit] is candid that this is a word match over added lines and not a reading of the change.

features.name: Re-review is incremental across visits
features.label: A "since your last look" filter, and a banner on the queue row saying how many changes landed since you approved.
features.promise: Per-reviewer state persists between visits, so a reviewer returning after the author has pushed again sees how many changes landed since they approved and can filter the diff to just those.
features.howToVerify: Approve a change as a reviewer, push further changes as the author, then return to screen 11 and confirm the queue row banners the number of changes since that approval, and that screen 12 offers a "since your last look" filter restricted to them.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:23, "Screens 11 and 12".
features.evidence: Per-reviewer state persists and both screens use it. Opening screen 12 recorded a look under my principal in the barn-review-base record ('looks': {pa5g3hz: {principal: local://user-btc48, packet, sha, at}}), which survived reloads and navigations. The queue row then carried the banner with the count: '2 commits and 1 uncommitted file since Default Admin approved this on 2026-08-24. Show only what changed since then', and the demo row carried its own ('6 uncommitted files since...'). On screen 12 [data-testid=rc-since-last-look] narrows the diff and states the relationship to the whole: 'Showing what has landed since <sha>, the commit you last read... The whole change, measured from the last published version, is 1 file. Approve still commits all of it.'

features.name: Two sign-offs by two different people
features.label: Splits "is it safe?" from "does it work?" — two questions, two people, neither able to answer the other's.
features.promise: The code review is signed by a developer and the outcome sign-off by the person who asked for the change; they are separate acts by separate roles, not one approval recorded twice.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the code review record (screen 12) and the verification record (screen 13) carry distinct signer identities and distinct timestamps, and that signing one does not mark the other complete.
features.notes: Rationale row 44:59; flow map 43:32 "A developer" and 43:37 "The person who asked"; cover point three 29:21 "a separate outcome sign-off by the person who asked".
features.evidence: The two records are separate objects with their own verdict, principal, name, timestamp and commit, and neither implies the other. Approving the code on screen 12 wrote signoffs.code and left the outcome row on screen 13 reading 'Outcome sign-off - you - in progress'; signing off the outcome later wrote a second entry with its own timestamp. Handing the criteria list back wrote outcome = changes-requested while code stayed approved, and requesting changes from the code review's decision bar wrote code = changes-requested while the outcome stayed approved - four combinations, all held independently. The roles are separated on the surfaces too: screen 13 tells the reviewer 'You are checking whether this does the job, not whether the code is any good. Reading the code is a separate step, on the review screen, and not this one', and the publish dialog labels the two 'Is it safe?' and 'Does it do the job?'. I could not reproduce the 'Needs a second signer' refusal this round because approving on screen 12 commits the working tree, which moves HEAD past the packet and makes both sign-offs stale before the dialog can compare their principals; the same-signer refusal was observed directly in the previous wave and the code path (`same-signer` in gateFrom/GATE_CHIPS) is unchanged.

Secondary text 16:869 reads 'metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 may change between Kubernetes minors — the panel will show an empty state if it disappears'.
features.defect: PublishModal.vue's `unstableCheck()` builds its sentence with `this.unstable.map((f) => `${f.api} (${f.path}:${f.line})`)` (pkg/barn/components/PublishModal.vue:790), but `scanUnstableApis()` returns `Finding` objects whose field is `what`, not `api` (pkg/barn/change-checks.ts:23-28 and :191). The credentials row two lines above uses `f.what` correctly, and screen 12's automated-checks column also uses `f.what` (pages/review-change.vue:3200), so this is the single wrong field reference. The check has only ever been seen green before, which is why it read as a pass.
features.evidence: Green state is right ('No unstable Kubernetes APIs added - The added lines name no alpha or beta group-version'). An alpha or beta group-version can change or disappear between Kubernetes minors...'. The group-version is printed as the literal word 'undefined'.

Fixture built by hand in barn-demo-extension the way publishExtension builds it: recordBaseline's exact shell wrote refs/barn/working-build at the clean HEAD tree with subject "Working build demo 0.0.1", then pages/Home.vue was modified and NEW-FILE-AFTER-BUILD.txt created so the failed tree was distinguishable. It is a ref in the extension's own repository, so it is the same point for everybody and it survives this tab. 2 changed files since." - so the durable ref, not sessionStorage, is what it resolved. Clicked it. Afterwards, in the pod: tag barn-snap/1787531269839 "the failed build before rolling back" exists and holds BOTH the modified Home.vue and the new file; the working tree's Home.vue is back to the working-build content with the probe line gone; sessionStorage barn.publish.failure is null and the screen has switched to its "No recent build failure" empty state. The safety snapshot is taken first and the restore is real. The pod was returned to exactly the state it was found in (clean tree, no refs/barn, no snapshot tags, one commit). Driven on the dev server at :8005; the code path is unchanged by this wave, so the installed bundle should behave identically.

features.evidence: Re-read against the current panel and it still refuses out loud, in the place the button would be: "There is no \"undo my request\" here. Nothing ties this failure to the request that caused it - the record holds the build's own output and no turn - and the per-turn file record the review screens read is blind to an edit made in the Terminal tab or through a shell command. Reversing \"the request\" would be reversing a guess. \"Undo the last change\" above is the honest neighbour: the most recently edited file, or the assistant's last committed turn when the tree is clean." features.howToVerify: Open the Studio settings screen (the gear in the rail, or /barn/settings if it exists), select 'Ask before every file edit', send a prompt in the editor and check the assistant stops for approval on each file write.
features.notes: Radio 21:851 is unfilled (not selected). Description 21:855 'Slowest, safest. You approve each write. Best while you are learning what Studio does.' One of three mutually exclusive options, so this setting is three-valued.
features.defect: Not selectable, so the promised behaviour cannot be produced from this page. It needs --dangerously-skip-permissions dropped from pod/claude-session.sh and a way for the terminal to surface claude's approval prompts. The workspace's own chip can cycle the running session, but claude's cycle has no "ask before every file edit" mode in it, so even that cannot reach this level.
features.evidence: The radio is rendered disabled and unchecked. detectPermission() reads the pod's own claude-session.sh and reports --dangerously-skip-permissions, so "Do not ask at all" is the row carrying the "In force" chip. The card's banner says outright that none of the three is settable.

features.name: Let the assistant edit files but ask before commands

features.notes: Radio 21:857 is filled with the brand green and the row is tinted green with a green border, so this is the current value. Description 21:861 'The assistant writes and rewrites extension files on its own, but stops before anything that touches the cluster.'
features.defect: Unchanged on this page. detectPermission() already recognises --permission-mode acceptEdits, so the card would follow the moment pod/claude-session.sh changed. The workspace chip can cycle the running session to "File edits apply, everything else asks" (I drove it), but that is a per-session cycle in the pod, not this card, and a restarted session comes back on the bundle's flag.
features.evidence: The radio is disabled and unchecked, and it is not the default: "Do not ask at all" is the one marked In force. So neither half of the promise holds.

features.name: Understand the scope of the permission setting

features.defect: Unchanged: the design's scope claim (per user, in force from the next message) does not hold. It is per pod and it takes effect when a session next starts. The page states the truth instead of the promise.
features.evidence: The card's banner opens "Not settable, and not per user." and explains that the flag is one line of claude-session.sh in the extension's seed ConfigMap, that Studio rewrites that ConfigMap from the bundle on every page load, and that everybody with a terminal in the pod is at the same level, reached when their session next starts.

features.name: Your part pill
features.label: Code review
features.promise: Each row says which kind of review is being asked of this user: 'Code review', 'Outcome sign-off' or 'Blocked'.

features.defect: The "Your part" column was deliberately removed (DEPARTURES.md #5). Each row still says which question is being asked, through its action button plus a chip on every row that is not an ordinary code review. Re-adding a "Code review" pill would duplicate the button beside it.
features.evidence: Settled by reading the promise and the departure against the current code. DEPARTURES.md #5 records the column's removal as a considered decision, and the removal stands - but its stated premise ("it rendered the same sentence on every row") is now imprecise, because review-queue.vue models four parts (partFor(): blocked, handover, outcome, code) and renders a chip for three of them: "Blocked" (lock), "Not handed over" (upload) and "Outcome sign-off" (eye). Only the ordinary code-review row carries no chip. Drove all four states to confirm that. So the accurate argument for the removal is the narrower one the code comment makes: the chip is reserved for the rows that are not the ordinary case, and on an ordinary row a "Code review" pill would say exactly what the button beside it already says. The action cell is the readout - actionLabel() returns "Open the brief" for blocked, "Sign off" for outcome and "Review" otherwise - so every row does say which of the two questions is being asked; it says it in the control rather than in a pill next to the control. The design's promise is stale in its literal form (a pill on every row, node 36:1089) and satisfied in substance. Nothing was changed.

features.name: Which prompt produced this hunk
features.label: Prompt 3 of 5
features.promise: Every diff hunk is labelled with the prompt that generated it, quoted verbatim, and when it ran.
features.howToVerify: Confirm each hunk carries a sparkle-marked provenance strip with 'Prompt N of 5', the quoted prompt and a relative time.
features.notes: Hunk 1: 'colour the bars by severity so a pressure event stands out', 2 hours ago. Hunk 2 (38:1317): 'show 24 hours of node conditions on the cluster page'.
features.defect: Two causes, both in the pod scripts rather than in the page. (1) barn-provenance.mjs resolves its tree with readdirSync('/app/pkg')[0], and demo's pod holds /app/pkg/base as well as /app/pkg/demo, so its report is about base: run by hand as 'cd /app/pkg/demo && node /seed/barn-provenance.mjs report' it answers base 195e23d5, which is /app/pkg/base's HEAD. Its Stop hook commits into base for the same reason, and shell.sh starts the pane's claude in /app/pkg/base with the same 'ls -d /app/pkg/*/ | head -1'. extensions.ts fixed exactly this in packageDir(name) and its comment names demo's pod as the case; the two pod scripts were not updated with it. (2) Even with the trees aligned, a hunk can only resolve after the turn's commit exists: report() counts a blame sha of all zeros as unrecorded, so the line an Edit just wrote is unattributable until the Stop hook commits it. The hand-over's own sweep commit ('Uncommitted work, swept in at the hand-over') carries no Barn-Turn trailer, so a change that is swept in rather than committed by a turn is permanently unattributable too.
features.evidence: With a signed-in claude, a recorded prompt, a Barn-Turn commit and an uncommitted hunk all present at once, screen 12 still could not label the hunk. /barn/review/demo/working showed one hunk for pages/Home.vue and its provenance strip read 'This file is not in the provenance report, so nothing is known about what produced it.' The packet-prompt panel showed the prompt verbatim with 'Prompt 1 of 1 ... 14 minutes ago · from the workspace screen · ended in no commit, so no line can be traced to it'.
